title: Veterinary Emergency & Critical Care
description: Theoretical and practical aspects of assisting the veterinarian in the management of medical and traumatic emergencies, with an emphasis on comprehensive nursing of critical patients. Recognition and assessment of cardiovascular shock, respiratory crisis, gastrointestinal emergency, and musculoskeletal trauma. Principles and techniques of fluid therapy and administration of emergency drugs. Application of treatment protocols for shock, cardiopulmonary arrest, gastrointestinal crisis, wounds and fractures, toxicoses, and various common emergencies. Explanation of the maintenance of emergency medical equipment and supplies. Intended for students in the Veterinary Technology Program; enrollment is limited to students accepted in the program.
outcomes: Identify cardiopulmonary arrest in patients and how to initiate and perform CPR effectively.
Recognize and discuss the history and clinical signs of veterinary emergency conditions including the pathophysiology and effects of shock.
objectives: Discuss the role of the veterinary technician in the care of emergency patients, including: initial patient assessment, application of diagnostic and therapeutic techniques, monitoring, and care and maintenance of emergency equipment
Describe the physiological mechanisms and effects of shock, and discuss the rationale treatment
List ways to recognize cardiopulmonary arrest and demonstrate techniques for cardiopulmonary resuscitation
Describe the pharmacological actions, indications, and methods of administration of various common emergency drugs
Demonstrate a problem-oriented approach to critical care nursing
Explain the recognition and treatment of respiratory emergencies
Explain the recognition and treatment of cardiovascular emergencies
Discuss appropriate interventions and management of toxicities
Discuss the recognition and treatment of gastrointestinal emergencies
Create a rational approach to the acute trauma patient
content: Role of the veterinary technician in emergency situations
Nature of veterinary emergencies and common examples
Initial patient assessment and recognition of emergencies
Monitoring of patient condition during and after treatment
Physical examination of the emergency patient
The art of triage: assessment and prioritization
Speaking with clients: phone and in-person triage
Primary and secondary survey of patient
Care and maintenance of emergency equipment and supplies
Causes of and classification of shock
Physiological mechanisms and consequences of shock
Drugs used in basic and advanced life support
Thoracocentesis, nasal catheters, and chest drains
Care of tracheostomy tubes, nasal catheters, and chest tubes
Recognition and treatment of common critical cardiac arrhythmias
